brief.headline: Navigating the Fragmenting Global Risk Landscape
brief.briefing_body: The dawn of September 25 brings a landscape of stark contrasts. While equity volatility remains low according to the VIX, we are witnessing significant divergence in the fixed-income and insurance sectors. The 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to 5.18%, reinforcing the 'higher-for-longer' interest rate regime. As noted in the Swiss Re Institute sigma No 2/2026 (July 2026), these persistent rates act as a stabilizer for investment income even as underwriting margins face pressure. We must remain vigilant regarding liquidity and cyber-physical threats, evidenced by the recent $351.6 million Bitget exchange hack. While catastrophe losses in the first half of 2026 remained below trend at $42 billion, the long-term upward trajectory of risk is intact. For our clients, asset resilience now requires hedging against both rising litigation costs and the inflationary impulse of a fragmenting world.
brief.source: Swiss Re sigma 2/2026 • Swiss Re H1 2026 cat-loss report • Swiss Re US P&C Outlook (Jul 2026) • Yahoo Finance • FRED • Insurance Journal, CNBC
